bull.b: Costco’s recurring membership fees and very high renewal rate provide a durable earnings foundation alongside merchandise sales. Growth in paid and executive memberships supports customer retention, repeat warehouse traffic, and the ability to sustain the low-price value proposition over time.

Improving operating and free cash flow gives Costco capacity to fund warehouse expansion, digital investment, dividends, and other capital needs internally. The sharp reduction in leverage further strengthens financial flexibility and lowers balance-sheet risk through changing retail conditions.

Strong digital growth broadens Costco’s reach beyond warehouse visits, while the planned store pipeline creates additional capacity for member acquisition and sales growth. Together, these investments reinforce the membership ecosystem and provide multiple durable avenues for expansion.

bear.b: Costco’s value-led pricing strategy and mix changes can constrain merchandise profitability even when sales remain strong. Persistent investment in lower prices, alongside greater exposure to lower-margin categories, could limit operating leverage and make earnings growth more dependent on volume.

Slower membership expansion could reduce the pace of new recurring fee revenue and make future sales growth more reliant on existing members’ spending. It may also challenge Costco’s ability to maintain recent comp momentum as it cycles easier comparisons and develops fewer new markets.

Capacity constraints at productive warehouses may prevent Costco from fully capturing incremental visits unless relocations or expansions are completed. Reliance on third-party delivery partners also leaves execution dependent on external capabilities and could require additional investment to maintain competitiveness.
